claims.text: High-resolution modulated DSC with advanced baseline correction and drop-calorimetry cross-validation can accurately and efficiently determine melting properties in single-phase high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method can determine liquid-phase volume change in single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Al0.5CoCrFeNi is an example of a well-characterized, compositionally and microstructurally homogeneous single-phase HEA suitable for the method.
Heating rates of approximately 1–2 °C/min provide the precise modulation needed to isolate the melting event.
Heating only from room temperature to the solidus temperature can capture an isolated melting event.
Time-resolved heat-flow signatures clearly delineate the endothermic melting peak.
The delineated melting peak serves as a proxy for the phase change and its associated enthalpic event.
Modulated DSC directly measures heat flow during melting.
Integration of the melting heat-flow signal yields the enthalpy of fusion.
Melting temperature combined with known molar heat capacities and corrections for configurational and vibrational contributions yields the entropy of fusion.
Parallel thermal-expansion measurements can determine the volume change at melting.
Cross-validation with drop calorimetry minimizes errors caused by DSC baseline correction.
The proposed method can determine melting temperature with approximately 1–2% error.
The proposed method can determine fusion enthalpy with uncertainty below 2–3%.
Fusion entropy and volume change can be measured with precision comparable to the 2–3% fusion-enthalpy uncertainty.
Traditional DSC without advanced baseline correction or independent verification often has roughly 5% error because of baseline drift and overlapping transitions.
The method is most applicable to HEAs with distinct, non-overlapping melting transitions.
Concurrent phase transitions and melting temperatures beyond the DSC operating range limit the method's effectiveness.
Residual uncertainty after cross-calibration is approximately 2–3%.

contradictions.description: The stated thermal cycle stops at the solidus temperature, while the method requires delineation and integration of the full melting peak to obtain fusion enthalpy and a complete fusion profile; reaching only the solidus generally does not encompass the entire melting interval.

The headline method attributes volume-change determination to mDSC plus drop calorimetry, but the mechanism requires an additional parallel thermal-expansion measurement that is absent from the stated intervention.
